name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,520

clue.text: Flying saucers circling Yemen's capital city

indicators.note: things sent flying are scattered, so the letters of the following word land in a new order
to circle something is to go all round it, so the rearranged letters wrap around another piece
a capital is the head letter of a word, so only the start of Yemen is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the opening letter of Yemen

explanation.surface: UFOs are reported orbiting the capital of Yemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying saucers' reads as one phrase about UFOs, but 'Flying' is the signal working on the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Syracuse is a historic city in Sicily, and also one in New York State.

clue.text: Work at length to stop secret agent becoming careless

indicators.note: at sets the work abbreviation next to the length abbreviation
to stop a gap is to plug it, so this pair goes inside the agent word

blocks.note: a spy is a secret agent; it is split to take the plug
L is the abbreviation for length
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A spy grows slack after a long assignment.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy means slapdash or lacking care in one's work, so it pairs with negligent.

clue.text: Left winger stymied by my best ever performance

indicators.note: stymied means blocked, so the exclamation sits in the way inside the political word

blocks.note: a Red is a left-wing socialist
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

explanation.surface: A footballer on the left wing is thwarted in a personal-best game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left winger' suggests football; here it is a political Red. 'My!' and cor are both exclamations.
explanation.definitionFit: A record is the best performance ever achieved, such as a world record time.

clue.text: Engaged in singing exam after church

indicators.note: after puts the exam word behind the church abbreviation

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A choirboy takes a spoken test after the Sunday service.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral means relating to a choir, so it describes music or people performing as a vocal group.

clue.text: Bewitched for a short time? Sure

blocks.note: a spell is a brief period, as in a spell of rain
bound means certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: A question and an answer: under a charm only briefly? Definitely.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellbound means held as if by magic, enchanted or completely captivated.

clue.text: Still in charge after position in society is reduced

indicators.note: something reduced has been cut down, so the phrase loses its closing letters
after places the abbreviation for in charge behind the shortened word

blocks.note: status is one's standing in society; it is then trimmed
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Someone stays in command even after a loss of social standing.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'reduced' trims two letters from the end, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Static describes something not moving or changing, the adjective sense of motionless or unmoving.

clue.text: Island's secret society involved in row taken aback? Just the opposite

indicators.note: taken aback puns on taken back, so the word for row is read from right to left
involved in means placed inside, which first suggests the society goes within the row
this phrase swaps the roles just described, so the outer and inner pieces trade places

blocks.note: a triad is a Chinese secret criminal society
a din is a noisy row; it is then reversed

explanation.surface: A secret society tangled up in a quarrel is shocked, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites a second reading, and 'Just the opposite' answers it by reversing which piece holds which.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger island of the Caribbean nation of Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Suppress article containing nonsense about lieutenant

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the lieutenant abbreviation faces the other way
containing means the article holds everything else inside it

blocks.note: the is the definite article
rot means rubbish or nonsense
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: An officer's silly report about a lieutenant is suppressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle is to choke or strangle, and figuratively to stifle or check something.

clue.text: Party to invite scorn

blocks.note: Con is the abbreviation for the Conservative Party
to tempt is to invite or entice

explanation.surface: Someone involved in an act that attracts derision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party to' reads as a single phrase meaning involved in; it splits as Party, then 'to', then invite.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is disdain or the feeling that something is worthless, a close synonym of derision.

clue.text: Formerly needing more than a quick appraisal

blocks.note: once means at some time in the past
over can mean in excess of, as in over fifty

explanation.surface: Something that used to take longer than a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: A once-over is a brief, rapid inspection or examination of someone or something.

clue.text: Companion not entirely accepting it's a fruit

indicators.note: not entirely means incomplete, so the friend word is cut short by its last letter
to accept something is to take it in, so the shortened word holds another piece inside

blocks.note: a crony is a close friend or companion; its tail is then dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend who only half agrees that something is a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' does double duty: 'it' is wordplay, and the 's joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A citron is a large, thick-skinned citrus fruit resembling a lemon, used mostly for candied peel.

clue.text: Easily transported by river on a piece of rough board

indicators.note: only a piece of the word rough is wanted, namely its opening letter
on signals pieces placed one against the next to build the word in sequence

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
the first letter of rough
board and table both mean meals provided, and a table is a flat board

explanation.surface: Something carried downstream floating on a rough plank.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable means light or compact enough to be carried around easily, which matches moved without effort.

clue.text: Not at all petty

blocks.note: first meaning: hardly at all
second meaning: small-minded or trivial

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a denial that someone is petty, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Little works as an adverb meaning scarcely, and as an adjective for minor, trivial or mean-spirited.

clue.text: Rees-Mogg finally abandoning common sense in support of fool's unjustified claim

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the name, so only its closing letter is wanted
abandoning means leaving behind, so that single letter is dropped from the word for common sense
in a down clue, a support sits underneath, so this piece goes below the fool

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
gumption is shrewd practical sense
the last letter of Rees-Mogg, taken out of the previous word

explanation.surface: A dig at the Tory politician: a fool backs a baseless claim lacking sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Rees-Mogg is a British Conservative politician. GUMPTION loses its G to give UMPTION, placed under ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: An assumption is something taken for granted without proof, so a groundless belief or claim.

clue.text: Nonsense to poke fun at small beer

blocks.note: to cod is an informal British verb for to tease or hoax
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
wallop is British slang for beer

explanation.surface: Mocking someone over their modest pint is silly talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Both COD (to kid) and WALLOP (beer) are informal British words.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop is British slang for rubbish talk, much like balderdash or tosh.

clue.text: Push forward from back of crowd to interrupt shocked tour rep

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the last letter of crowd is kept
to interrupt is to break in, so this letter breaks into the reworked letters
shocked suggests being jolted out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the final letter of crowd

explanation.surface: Someone shoves forward from the back of a crowd to cut in on a startled holiday guide.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to stick out or project beyond a surface, extending outwards.

clue.text: In pursuit of the total amount in spite of everything

blocks.note: to be after something is to pursue it
all means the whole quantity

explanation.surface: Chasing the full sum regardless of the obstacles.
explanation.definitionFit: After all is an idiom meaning nevertheless, despite what has happened or been said.

clue.text: Rector gets Yoko to cut jokes from parts of speech

indicators.note: gets signals that the rector abbreviation is joined by the next piece
to cut is to slice into, so this pair sits inside the word for jokes

blocks.note: puns are jokes on words; the word is split for the insertion
R is the abbreviation for rector
Yoko Ono, the artist married to John Lennon

explanation.surface: A vicar asks Yoko to edit out some wordplay from a grammar lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronouns such as he, she and they are a word class, one of the grammatical categories.

clue.text: Judge by repeated hesitation to embrace result of people's vote

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the two hesitation sounds wrap round another piece

blocks.note: a ref (referee) judges a game
two hesitation noises, ER and UM, one after the other
an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: Someone stammers and hesitates while weighing up the outcome of a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: The two hesitation noises are different ones and split apart to do the embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: A referendum is a direct ballot of the whole electorate on one question, popularly dubbed a people's vote.

clue.text: Casual worker from the outskirts of Jaipur receiving award without a hint of boastfulness

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outer letters of the city name are kept
receiving means taking in, so the outer pair holds the honour inside
without in its old sense of outside, so the honour goes round the letter that follows
a hint is just a trace, so only the first letter of boastfulness is used

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Jaipur, split apart
the OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire
the first letter of boastfulness

explanation.surface: An odd-job worker near Jaipur is honoured and stays perfectly modest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside: OBE wraps round B to give OBBE, which sits inside J...R.
explanation.definitionFit: A jobber is someone who does odd jobs or piecework rather than holding a steady post.

clue.text: One easily deceived by lawyer's letter

blocks.note: a lamb is a meek, innocent and trusting person
a DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A gullible client is conned by a solicitor's correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence but means a character of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh character of the Greek alphabet, written as an upside-down V.

clue.text: Courage of the French experienced by them initially at the front

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of them is used
at the front places these pieces ahead of the French article

blocks.note: to have met something is to have experienced it
the first letter of them
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French bravery is first felt by those in the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle means spirit or resilience in facing difficulty, the nerve to cope well.

clue.text: Connections in Iceland accommodating a German tenor earlier

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the country code houses another piece
earlier says the tenor abbreviation comes first, ahead of everything else

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor
IS is the international code for Iceland
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: An Icelandic venue puts up a German tenor ahead of others.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-ins are links or associations between things, such as a book tied to a film.

clue.text: Aware of heartless Italian poet becoming fashionable

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the poet's name is removed

blocks.note: to be up to someone's tricks is to be wise to or aware of them
Dante Alighieri wrote the Divine Comedy; his middle letter goes

explanation.surface: Knowing about a cold Italian poet who comes into vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: DANTE has five letters, so its heart is the N, leaving DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-to-date means modern or current, in keeping with the latest trends and styles.

clue.text: Ancient city originally associated by students with a mythological god

indicators.note: originally points to the very beginning, so only the first letter of associated is kept

blocks.note: Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia
the first letter of associated
the NUS is the UK's National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Students linking an ancient city with a figure from myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranus is the Greek sky god, father of the Titans, who personified the heavens.

clue.text: Gradually getting through in small pieces

indicators.note: in places the word for through within the pair of small pieces

blocks.note: a bit is a small piece
by can mean through or by way of, as in by post
the plural yields a second small piece

explanation.surface: Working through something one small portion at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: Small pieces gives two BITs, and BY sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bit by bit means step by step, slowly and in stages over time.

clue.text: Sign up new clients first off

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter is taken away
new suggests the remaining letters are made over into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, then trimmed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A business asks newly arrived customers to register before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to enrol or join up, especially for military service.

clue.text: Profit from popular event split by Greer evenly

indicators.note: evenly picks out only the even-numbered letters of the surname
something split has a gap opened in it, into which another piece is set

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
a case is an instance or occurrence, as in 'in that event' or 'in that case'
the second and fourth letters of Greer

explanation.surface: Gains from a well-attended event are divided equally by someone called Greer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evenly' looks like it means equally in the surface, but it picks out the even-placed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is a growth or gain in amount, so a profit counts as one.
